sources.title: SFPUC · Drain clearing equipment and safety
sources.finding: Surface clearing uses a reflective vest, gloves and a rake, broom, shovel or grabber. Supplies are limited. Do not lift grates, enter ponding water or clear during a storm; report complete clogs and hazardous waste to 311.

sources.title: SF Public Works · Sandbag pickup
sources.finding: Residents and businesses with flood-prone properties may collect up to 10 free sandbags with proof of address, Monday–Saturday 8am–2pm, at the operations yard's Marin/Kansas gate. Self-loading and transport are required; current stock is not confirmed.

sources.title: San Francisco · Winter Storm & Flood Annex
sources.published: 2016-08-18; role document, not a live roster
sources.finding: Public Works handles pre-storm clearing, tree/debris response and specialist contractors; DBI assesses structural damage; SFPUC supports drainage; SFPD/SFMTA control access; SFFD/SFPW/SFPUC can support water removal. This establishes request owners, not available crew or equipment counts.

sources.title: SF.gov · Report a damaged or fallen tree
sources.locator: When to report; What to do
sources.finding: Report obstructing or damaged trees through 311. The published response range is 1–90 days, not guaranteed pre-storm availability. Call 911 for incidents involving power lines, vehicles or buildings.

sources.title: PG&E · Storm safety and outage reporting
sources.locator: Watch out for downed power lines
sources.finding: Treat downed lines as energized, stay away, call 911 and then PG&E at 1-800-743-5002. Public line maps do not authorize local crews to work on electrical infrastructure.

sources.title: DataSF · mapped catch basins and drains
sources.finding: Point geometry and asset identifiers locate a candidate inlet. Proximity to a historic flood report does not establish hydraulic connectivity or current blockage.

resources.name: Surface-clearing kit
resources.owner: Crew stores / SFPUC Adopt a Drain
resources.contents: Reflective vest, gloves, rake or broom, debris bags and disposal access
resources.availability: Confirm each crew's kit before leaving. SFPUC supplies some adopters, but availability is limited.

resources.name: Drainage crew and sewer equipment
resources.contents: Qualified response to below-grate blockages, sewer backups and street flooding
resources.availability: Request with the observed location and condition; no dedicated crew or response time is committed to this plan.

resources.name: Arborist and tree-removal equipment
resources.contents: Arborist assessment; saw, lift or removal equipment only when the assessment calls for it
resources.availability: Not counted as a general crew. Use 311 for a current public-tree concern; emergency escalation when wires, vehicles or buildings are involved.

resources.name: Building operator and structural engineer
resources.owner: Property owner; DBI for building-safety concerns
resources.contents: Access, maintenance records, glazing contractor and engineer-designed stabilization where necessary
resources.availability: Obtain the owner's current findings and arrange qualified inspection; no engineer or repair materials are assumed on site.

resources.name: Utility crew and building electrician
resources.contents: Utility isolation and line repair; compatible building backup, switchgear and load testing
resources.availability: Utility work requires PG&E. Building backup requires an electrician and owner-approved connection; no portable generator or fuel stock is assumed.

resources.name: Traffic control and alternate access
resources.contents: Authorized closure, signs, barriers and verified emergency/accessible route
resources.availability: General crews report conditions; traffic authority must authorize controls. No closure crew or barrier stock is committed.

resources.name: Sandbags and transport
resources.owner: Public Works operations yard, Marin / Kansas gate
resources.contents: Up to 10 free bags per eligible SF address; bring address proof and a vehicle for self-loading
resources.availability: Published pickup Monday–Saturday 8am–2pm. Stock and storm-specific hours need confirmation. A 30-minute plan must not assume collection and fitting will finish.

resources.name: Pumps and fitted flood barriers
resources.owner: Property operator / qualified contractor; emergency agency support where warranted
resources.contents: Site-compatible pump, safe discharge, reliable power and barrier matched to entry path
resources.availability: Request after inspecting the entry path, backflow and power. No pump capacity, barrier size or delivery time is inferred.
